pr.title: Plan Codex watch delivery while preserving Claude support
pr.head: c9420ae2b5b52af38ddc93cbdf5c75ccbc1fcc2f

summary: Projector's watch daemon is one background process per machine. It polls GitHub for the pull requests that agent sessions review or fix, and it writes each piece of new work, such as a new head to review or a finding to fix, as an event line in the owning session's events file. In Claude Code, Projector's mod reads that file and submits the lines as a prompt, which starts a turn even when the conversation is idle. Codex has no such adapter. The skills tell a Codex session to run project watch stream in the background, but printing a line does not start a turn in an idle Codex conversation.

This pull request adds a plan, at status ready, for a Codex adapter inside the existing daemon. Codex plugin hooks register the session and acknowledge each delivered batch. The daemon wakes the session with codex queue --thread <id> --message <batch> --resume, a Codex CLI command that queues a message for an existing session and loads the session if it is not loaded. Claude Code's mod, the stream fallback, and the one shared skill tree stay as they are. The pull request adds no code.
The Projector review of this head is clean, with no finding threads. It lists three suggestions for the plan, which the notes on the plan below repeat where they apply.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Watch daemon. The process that project watch serve runs. It polls GitHub and writes events for each session.
  • Session. One agent conversation, named by its id. Its folder under the daemon's state root holds its subscriptions and its events.
  • Deliverer. What moves a session's events into its conversation: mod in Claude Code, stream elsewhere, and in this plan codex.
  • Lapse. A mod or stream session that has not renewed for five minutes stops counting as live, and the daemon stops polling for it.
  • Batch. In this plan, up to 8 KiB of event lines that the daemon claims and queues to Codex as one message, marked PROJECTOR WATCH <batch-id>.

cards.title: What the plan decides
cards.html:
• Identity. The hook's session_id is both the watch session and the codex queue target. A subagent's hooks carry its parent's id, so workers never become delivery targets.
  • Lease. A Codex registration stays live for 24 hours after the last host activity, by wall clock, while it has subscriptions or pending events. SessionEnd ends it.
  • One batch at a time. Each session has at most one unacknowledged batch. A UserPromptSubmit hook acknowledges the batch whose marker it sees.
  • Uncertain submissions stop. Exit zero counts as queued. A timeout or crash during submission stops automatic retries until project watch codex-retry resends the batch.
  • Deferred. Remote app servers, credentials, scheduled tasks, and an MCP service.

groups.title: The Codex delivery plan
groups.kicker: A child plan of the watch daemon that adds a third deliverer for Codex
intro: The plan is one new file, a child of the watch-daemon plan. It is at status ready, which in this repository claims that every question blocking implementation is answered or deliberately deferred. The plan has no open question, and it names what it defers.

Read § 2.1 first. It walks one event from the hook that registers the session to the prompt that acknowledges the batch. § 2.2 gives the files each step writes under the session's folder, and § 4 gives one acceptance check per failure the design guards against.

checks.text: project check at this head prints Project plans are valid., project show watch-daemon/codex-delivery reports ready and now, and git diff --check over the pull request's range prints nothing.

files.note: The whole plan: problem, runtime flow, state files, components, reasons, acceptance checks, and cost.

checks.text: The plan's statements about the current code hold at this head. watch.DELIVERERS is ("mod", "stream"), LAPSE is 300 seconds, stream renews every 30 seconds, forget_sessions deletes a folder after seven days, and run_watch starts the daemon before every command but serve and stop.

All four links resolve. The Codex CLI reference documents --thread, --message, and --resume, and says that codex queue exits successfully when it cannot resume the session. The hooks page says that subagent hooks carry the parent's session_id.

The parent plan restarts a dead daemon with the next project watch command, which the mod runs within a minute. An idle Codex session runs no command until a hook fires, and this section does not say what restarts the daemon during the 24-hour lease. The review lists this as a suggestion.

The daemon words a reminder differently from the first announcement, for example FINDING … (still open). Coalescing only identical lines therefore keeps one stored copy of each standing item while a batch waits, and delivers it after the acknowledgment. The review lists this as a suggestion.
